_readme: Runtime + server configuration. Values are portable on purpose:
${VAR} and ${VAR:-fallback} are expanded from the environment at startup (see .env.example),
a leading ~ is expanded to your home directory,
{placeholder} is filled in per agent by the server (model, effort, sessionId, name, prompt, ...).
A {placeholder} with no value is dropped together with the option flag in front of it, so leaving
a default unset simply means the CLI's own default is used.
Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored by the server.

claude.label: Claude Code CLI
claude._envNote: The Claude CLI inherits the control room's environment minus every variable whose name contains KEY, TOKEN or SECRET, except the names in keepEnv (the CLI's own authentication). Add a name there only if the agent really needs that credential (e.g. GITHUB_TOKEN for gh).
claude._note: Needs the `claude` CLI on PATH and already signed in (run `claude` once in a terminal). The first launch in a new folder shows Claude Code's trust prompt; answer it in the agent's Terminal tab - the control room does not auto-accept it.
claude._defaultsNote: model and effort are deliberately unset, so every agent uses the CLI's own default model. Pin them here if you want to: "model" takes an alias or a full model name, "effort" takes low|medium|high|xhigh|max. Run `claude --help` to see what your CLI version accepts.

deepseek.label: DeepSeek Harness (headless)
deepseek._note: DSH_REPO points at your DeepSeek Harness checkout and defaults to ~/deepseek-harness. Override it with the DSH_REPO environment variable, or replace this whole runtime with any other CLI that takes the prompt as its last argument.
deepseek._envNote: Worker processes inherit the control room's environment minus every variable whose name contains KEY, TOKEN or SECRET, except the names listed in keepEnv. Add a name there only if that worker really needs the credential.

external.label: External session (not spawned by the control room)

codex.label: Codex CLI (ChatGPT)
codex._envNote: The Codex CLI inherits the control room's environment minus every variable whose name contains KEY, TOKEN or SECRET, except the names in keepEnv (the CLI's own authentication). Add a name there only if the agent really needs that credential (e.g. GITHUB_TOKEN for gh).
codex._note: Run codex once to sign in using your existing ChatGPT plan or supported CLI credentials. No model or effort is forced: CLI configuration applies. Model-specific effort availability is enforced by the CLI. New sessions receive a CLI-generated ID discovered from their local rollout; restarts resume that ID. Sandbox mode does not bypass approval prompts.
